translations.text: Rebuke him in his place [?]. This too is the way in which someone is [?]; even more so is the person among you who will say, “God will forgive those who do, or will do, those abominable deeds in his congregations after they have learned all this knowledge and all these words.”

For it is easier, you people who have desired this because of the impurity of your souls, for the one who tells you these things to be in harmony with tax collectors, prostitutes, and all the wicked, if they turn away from their unjust or filthy deeds, than to be in harmony with you, because you are turning yourselves away from purity and truthful deeds toward filth and dishonest deeds.

Was it not rather out of extreme anger over those who had also committed corrupt deeds before today that I said these words on a day of distress, when we were gathered together: “Am I to assemble or offer the offering with impure people who commit corrupt deeds?”
Or how difficult is it for someone who speaks the truth to assemble with tax collectors, prostitutes, and all the wicked, or to offer the offering with them?

[?] Not because they have turned away from their evil deeds—or rather, because they have not turned away from them—but because no judgment falls upon him if he assembles or offers the offering with them. For they have not been entrusted to him, so that he should be questioned about them.

How, in turn, will it not be difficult for someone to whom people have been entrusted to assemble with impure people who commit corrupt deeds among them, or to offer offerings with them, when their blood and their judgment fall upon him?

But their judgment and their blood fall upon the council of leaders, because not only is the soul of the one who gives them orders not in harmony with those who commit that evil among you, but it has also been prescribed for him, through the rule and the counsel ordained by God, as it has been from the beginning until now, not to eat bread or drink water, or assemble with the whole congregation to pray, or present the offering, until he places their judgment upon their own heads and their blood upon the crowns of their heads,
because someone might again dare to commit such abominable deeds in the Lord’s congregations, among our holy brothers who guard themselves against every defilement and every deceitful deed.

It will not be as it has often been within you, congregation, with disturbances, retreats, and harsh actions, either this time or during the other days that the one who speaks the truth will spend alive. Rather, those who are revealed to him to have committed corrupt deeds within you he will exclude from you without disturbance and without shouting.

And if there are others within you who deceitfully commit abominable deeds without being known to us, whether male or female, great or small, they are left in the hands of God’s wrath, for him to punish them in his anger.

For those whom you do not know to be committing corrupt deeds within you—the curses themselves that are written in the Scriptures, and the curses in the books written for us, know them and how to act against them with all their torments. The pieces of the belts and bandages that this man laid aside after they had been tied around him, because they did not help him, or because they became useless, or because they have no use—as you will see some of them in one condition at one time, another portion in another condition, another portion like this, and another portion like that—are so that you will understand, brothers, that this man did not bind himself with this great quantity of wrappings or bandages for any other reason except the matter that he himself knows.

If the bandages or belts that have worn out and can no longer help me or be used to bind me during the illness in my body, or the body, are numerous in the eyes of someone who knows their number, the belts or bandages that you will see laid aside, having no use, are more numerous than those that became useless. But they will seem few to you, because it is impossible to tell from their deteriorated appearance which is which, or this one from that one, so that someone could count them or state their number.

And they will be in the place [?]—I myself do not know who it is—who hid them there beneath the earth, in the place where the abyss, or the abysses, opened, filled with every useless thing, until the time when you see them with your own eyes.

For everything that this man who is speaking to you, congregation, did before today, he did because he wanted to remove the shame from those who do these corrupt deeds among us, turning it back upon himself, because he loves his neighbor as himself.
But now he himself is removing it from himself and turning it back upon everyone who does or will do abominable things deceitfully or secretly, whether male or female.
And their shame is upon them, for it rests upon them and is plainly visible upon them, and they are exposed as having it upon them.
And honoring them again in the presence of this man who is now distressed [?], in the same way—especially a blow with a staff in his hand—from today onward is a shame to him himself.

This statement is not about my esteemed brothers or beloved children, because of their purity and their love for God. Rather, it concerns those whom this holy place does not benefit and who gain no benefit in it, because they are destroying their hope, as we said earlier.
Were not these places, or every congregation gathered in them because of God's name, called holy places?
Then how cursed will those be who defile them with shameful deeds!
Or was this saying not enough for those miserable wretches, when it cut them off from life once and for all: “The children who have become defiled are not his”?
Or is there still greater wrath than this that God will bring upon whoever destroys his temple: “Whoever destroys God's temple, God will destroy him”?

What is easy [?] down to [?] those who fear God in these congregations? With what will he be able to honor them, or with what will he be able to bless them, beyond what the saints said: “Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways.”
You will eat the fruits of your labors.

But the one who is distressed over those who commit abominable deeds in these congregations at all times will disgrace them even more than what the saints said in anger: “The person who does not fear God will be in eternal places [?], with no one to seek him out.”

A man whom those who live within you, congregation, have often heard swearing, “I would rather die, or have God call me to account, than hear that someone is doing corrupt deeds within you”—is it not clear that he is innocent of this judgment and of the blood of those who afflict him, since they were not ashamed to do those abominable, ungodly deeds within you?
Oh, what will this place do?
Where will this place go?

Before today, the person who knew, or those who knew, the measure, or those who measured the evil things they had done within you, [?] will say [?]. They have already said that these things reached the thighs of those who did them, or indeed rose above them like a vast mire, and they sank into it like animals, although God planted us in it in his mercy.

But now, at this time, those who measure it or take its measure will say, or are saying, that it reaches the knees [?], and indeed it does not reach [?]. And those who fell into it, or onto it, sank up to their thighs.
Indeed, it is not like that within you now either.
May it never happen!
Nor was there much of it.

But those who fell into it wallowed in it like pigs, not merely until it reached their thighs, or until they sank into it up to their thighs, but until they appeared filthy and smeared with it, from their toenails to the hair on their heads.

If that mud had been deeper at this present time, or if it still reached the thighs according to its former depth, those who saw the people in it would have said, “Certainly they could not get up or come out of it, because it is deep.”
And whoever says that it has not diminished very, very greatly is like someone who sheds blood, because he has insulted the grace that the Lord Jesus Christ has shown us.
But in the final period, in turn, they would not say that the mud reached the ankles, or the knees, or the thighs, but the necks of those who do corrupt deeds in it, whether male or female.

Furthermore, this other expression, “measure” or “take a measurement,” is not only written at the beginning of the first document that was set down originally, measuring or taking the measure of what exists or what happened within you, congregation. Rather, it also says there, “They took account of what you did not know or understand,” and, “They took account of what stirred you up”—those who came to learn about or see the things that happened within you, in the deep and hidden places that are filled with darkness, or are darkness within you.

But if someone asks, “What are these measurements, or this taking of measurements? Who were those who took measurements? Or what did they measure?” let him tell us, or let him tell me, [?] how the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was measured with a reed, who measured it, and why they measured it or marked out its boundaries. Was it, then, in sorrow,

or rather in greater reassurance? And again, why did Zechariah the prophet say, “I will take two staffs for myself, calling one Beauty and the second Cord”? And was it, then, in mercy and compassion, or rather in greater anger and wrath, that he said afterward, “I will take my beautiful staff and throw it away, to break the covenant that I established with all the peoples”?

And they will be destroyed in those days, and the Canaanites, the sheep who pay attention to me, will [?] that it is a word of the Lord. Then again: “I cast away the second staff, Cord, to destroy the covenant in the midst of Judah and in the midst of Jerusalem.”
And again, whether in consolation or rather in rebuke, Micah the prophet also said: “They measured out my people's portion with a measuring line for a field.”

And whether those who measured that portion were from God, like the one who measured the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, and as with the designation of the two staffs, Beauty and Cord, which we mentioned earlier, or whether they were from...
